findings.raw_candidate_behaviour: Version B contains two migrations with numeric prefix 129 and the migration runner records only filenames, not content hashes.
findings.expected_behaviour: Migration identity must be unambiguous and already-applied migrations must fail closed on content mismatch.
findings.reproduction: List backend/src/db/migrations/129_*.sql and inspect backend/src/db/migrate.ts schema_migrations tracking columns.
findings.root_cause: Two independently developed lineages allocated prefix 129 and the existing runner predated content-hash tracking.
findings.impact: Upgrade paths can be hard to reason about and changed migration contents could be accepted as already applied.
findings.remediation: Version C adds migration content-hash/sequence tracking and a migration identity ledger with an explicit duplicate-prefix compatibility contract.
findings.remaining_risk: Existing databases with legacy null content_hash values are backfilled on first Version C migration run; historical content before that point cannot be independently reconstructed from schema_migrations alone.

findings.raw_candidate_behaviour: PR #26 merged generated route and inventory artifacts after Batch 06A generated artifacts.
findings.expected_behaviour: Generated reports must be refreshed and checked by release-gate rather than trusted by merge status.
findings.reproduction: Run make release-gate on Version B or Version C.
findings.root_cause: Generated ledgers are line-specific and can drift when two large branches are merged.
findings.impact: A stale report could overstate current repository state if release-gate is not run.
findings.remediation: No code remediation in the Version C freeze; this is enforced by existing release-gate and generated-report freshness checks during Batch 07 verification.
findings.remaining_risk: Any later generated-artifact change must be committed only after the underlying generator succeeds.
